title: AI Agents that Work
outcome: Design, build, evaluate and operate agentic systems that do real multi-step work reliably enough to trust with something that matters.

phases.name: Agent Foundations
phases.outcome: Understand what an agent is mechanically, and build one that does real work in a loop.

modules.name: What an Agent Actually Is
modules.objective: Describe the loop that separates an agent from a single model call.
lessons: What the model decides and what your code decides
Where agents genuinely beat a single call
Where an agent is the wrong shape entirely
practice: Judge eight tasks as agent-shaped or not
lab: Write the loop by hand, no framework
A minimal working loop you wrote yourself, with each part explained

modules.name: Tools
modules.objective: Define tools a model can call correctly on the first attempt.
lessons: A tool is a function with a description for a reader
Writing a description that prevents misuse
Parameters, schemas and the argument it invents
Return values the model can act on
Too many tools, and the choice that gets worse
practice: Rewrite eight bad tool definitions
lab: Build a tool set an agent uses without errors
A tool set with a log showing correct selection across twenty runs

modules.name: Controlling the Loop
modules.objective: Decide when an agent continues, stops, or asks — and enforce it in code.
lessons: Stopping conditions you set, not ones it chooses
Step limits, time limits and cost limits
Detecting a loop that's going nowhere
Asking the human: when and how
practice: Set control policy for seven agent tasks
lab: Add full loop control to your agent
An agent with enforced limits, loop detection and a working resume

modules.name: Errors Inside the Loop
modules.objective: Handle tool failures so the agent recovers instead of confabulating.
lessons: What the model does when a tool errors
Error messages written for the model to act on
The agent that reports success after a failure
practice: Design error handling for eight tool failures
lab: Make your agent survive a hostile tool layer
An agent that completes or fails honestly against tools that error randomly

modules.name: Your First Real Agent
modules.objective: Build an agent that completes a genuinely useful multi-step task.
lessons: Choosing a task worth an agent
Watching it run and reading the trace
Deciding whether it earned its complexity
practice: Critique seven agent designs
lab: Build an agent that does one real job
A working agent with a run trace and an honest verdict on whether it beats a script

phases.name: Planning and Reasoning
phases.outcome: Get agents to decompose work, choose strategies, and adapt when the plan meets reality.

modules.name: Decomposition
modules.objective: Break a goal into steps that can be executed and verified independently.
lessons: Plan first, then execute: what it buys
Steps with a checkable completion condition
Dependencies and what can run in parallel
practice: Decompose seven goals into verifiable plans
lab: Build a plan-then-execute agent
An agent that produces a plan, executes it, and reports per-step outcomes

modules.name: Choosing an Approach
modules.objective: Make an agent pick a sensible strategy rather than the first one it thought of.
lessons: The first approach is not the best approach
Knowing when to abandon an approach
Recording why an approach was chosen
practice: Evaluate seven strategy selections
lab: Add strategy selection to your agent
An agent that considers alternatives and logs its reasoning per choice

modules.name: Self-Checking
modules.objective: Build checking into a run without it becoming self-congratulation.
lessons: Asking an agent to check its own work
Critic and worker as separate roles
Checks that cost less than the mistake
practice: Design verification for eight agent outputs
lab: Add a real critic step to your agent
An agent whose critic demonstrably rejects bad output on seeded failures

modules.name: Adapting to Reality
modules.objective: Handle the situation where the world isn't what the plan assumed.
lessons: The plan meets the actual environment
Detecting that an assumption was wrong
Partial success and what to keep
practice: Handle seven broken-assumption scenarios
lab: Test your agent against a changed environment
A run record showing the agent detecting and adapting to three seeded changes

modules.name: More Than One Agent
modules.objective: Decide when multiple agents help, and coordinate them without chaos.
lessons: When one agent is genuinely not enough
Passing context between agents without losing it
Independent perspectives that aren't just duplicates
The cost multiplier nobody budgets for
practice: Judge seven multi-agent designs against a single agent
lab: Build a two-role agent system and compare it
A working system plus a measured comparison against the single-agent version

phases.name: Memory and Context
phases.outcome: Give agents access to the right information at the right moment, at a cost you can afford.

modules.name: Context Engineering
modules.objective: Decide what goes into the model's view at each step and what stays out.
lessons: Context is a budget you spend every step
What must be present versus what can be fetched
Position, ordering and what gets ignored
Measuring what your context is costing
practice: Rebuild seven bloated contexts
lab: Halve your agent's context without losing quality
Before-and-after token counts with quality measured on a fixed test set

modules.name: Retrieval
modules.objective: Fetch the right information from a corpus at the moment the agent needs it.
lessons: Chunking, and the chunk that lost its meaning
practice: Diagnose eight retrieval failures
lab: Build and evaluate a retrieval layer
A retrieval layer with measured precision and recall on your own query set

modules.name: Long-Term Memory
modules.objective: Let an agent remember across runs without accumulating garbage.
lessons: Retrieving the memory that's relevant now
practice: Decide what to store for seven agents
lab: Add memory with an explicit forgetting policy
A memory layer with write rules, retrieval rules and a working expiry policy

modules.name: State and Durability
modules.objective: Make long runs survive restarts, crashes and days off.
practice: Make seven step designs safely resumable
lab: Make a long run survive being killed
A run killed at three different points that resumed correctly each time

modules.name: Grounding and Citation
modules.objective: Make an agent's claims traceable to a source you can check.
lessons: Citations that are real and locatable
practice: Audit eight grounded outputs for real support
lab: Add citation checking to your agent
A checker that catches unsupported claims, tested against seeded fabrications

phases.name: Real Systems
phases.outcome: Build the agent types people actually pay for, and prove one of them works end to end.

modules.name: Research Agents
modules.objective: Build an agent that gathers and synthesises information you can trust.
lessons: What makes research hard for an agent
Search, read, synthesise as separate stages
practice: Critique seven research agent outputs
lab: Build a research agent with verified citations
A research agent whose citations you spot-checked, with the error rate reported

modules.name: Coding Agents
modules.objective: Build an agent that changes code and verifies its own work.
lessons: Reading a codebase before changing it
Making a change and running the tests
The agent that deletes the failing test
Scope control on a code-changing agent
practice: Identify the guardrail missing in seven coding agents
lab: Build a coding agent that can't cheat
An agent that fixes a real bug with verification it cannot bypass

modules.name: Data and Workflow Agents
modules.objective: Build agents that process real volumes of data or drive a business workflow.
lessons: Per-item failure without losing the batch
Reporting on a batch a human must review
practice: Design batch handling for seven workflows
lab: Build a batch agent with validation
An agent processing 500 items with per-item outcomes and a review report

modules.name: Agents That Talk to People
modules.objective: Build a user-facing agent that knows its limits and hands over well.
lessons: What a user-facing agent must never do
Saying "I don't know" convincingly and correctly
Vulnerable users and the duty that creates
Measuring whether it actually helped anyone
practice: Judge eight user-facing agent responses
lab: Build a support agent with real escalation
An agent that escalates correctly on ten scenarios it should not handle

modules.name: Capstone — An Agent Worth Trusting
modules.objective: Build, evaluate, deploy and defend one agent that does something real.
lessons: Choosing a task that justifies an agent
Designing for verification from the start
Building, evaluating and iterating on evidence
Deploying with controls and cost limits
practice: Answer seven hard challenges to your design
lab: Deliver the capstone agent
A deployed agent with an eval set, measured results, cost per run, controls and a written defence

phases.name: Running Agents in Production
phases.outcome: Deploy an agent, control what it costs, watch what it does, and stay in control of it.

modules.name: Deploying
modules.objective: Run an agent somewhere other than your machine, safely.
lessons: Where a long-running agent actually runs
Secrets and credentials for an autonomous process
Isolation and what it can reach in production
Rolling out a change to something already running
practice: Choose the deployment shape for seven agents
lab: Deploy your agent with proper isolation
A deployed agent with least-privilege credentials and a documented blast radius

modules.name: Cost Control
modules.objective: Keep an autonomous system from spending money without limit.
lessons: Where the tokens actually go in a run
Cheaper models for the cheap steps
The runaway loop and the bill it produces
practice: Find the cost sink in seven run traces
lab: Cut your agent's cost per run in half
Before-and-after cost with quality held constant on your eval set

modules.name: Seeing What It Did
modules.objective: Instrument runs so you can reconstruct any one of them afterwards.
lessons: Tracing a run: every step, input and output
What to log and what never to log
Finding the run that went wrong among thousands
Alerts worth having on an autonomous system
Debugging a run from three weeks ago
practice: Diagnose eight runs from traces alone
lab: Add tracing and diagnose a seeded failure
A trace system plus a diagnosis made using only the trace

modules.name: Keeping Control
modules.objective: Keep a human meaningfully in control of a system that acts on its own.
lessons: Actions that must never be automatic
Approval steps that people actually read
The off switch and who can reach it
Auditability: proving what it did and why
Agents acting on behalf of other people
practice: Set the approval boundary for eight agents
lab: Add human-in-the-loop controls to your agent
Working approval gates plus a tested kill switch

modules.name: Operating It Over Time
modules.objective: Keep an agent working over months as models, tools and the world change.
lessons: Drift: it stopped working and nothing changed
Tool and API changes underneath you
A maintenance routine that fits a bad month
practice: Diagnose seven degradation reports
lab: Write your agent's operations runbook
A runbook covering monitoring, common failures, migration and shutdown

phases.name: Evaluating Agents
phases.outcome: Know whether an agent works, measure it repeatedly, and catch regressions before users do.

modules.name: What "Works" Means Here
modules.objective: Define success for a non-deterministic multi-step system in checkable terms.
lessons: It worked when I tried it is not evidence
Defining success per task, in advance
Outcome, process and cost as three measures
Variance: the same input, different runs
How many runs before you believe a number
practice: Write success criteria for seven agent tasks
lab: Define and document your agent's success criteria
Written criteria specific enough for someone else to score a run

modules.name: Building an Eval Set
modules.objective: Assemble cases that expose real weaknesses rather than confirming success.
lessons: Cases from real failures, not from imagination
Covering the boring, the hard and the adversarial
Keeping a set honest as you fix things
practice: Build eval cases for seven agents
lab: Build a thirty-case eval set
An eval set with expected outcomes and a documented sourcing rationale

modules.name: Grading Output
modules.objective: Score agent output automatically in a way that agrees with human judgement.
lessons: Exact match, and everything it can't grade
Rubrics a grader can apply consistently
Grading process, not just final answer
practice: Design graders for eight output types
lab: Build a grader and validate it against your own judgement
A grader with measured agreement against fifty hand-scored examples

modules.name: Catching Regressions
modules.objective: Notice when a change made things worse, including a change you didn't make.
lessons: Running evals as part of your workflow
The prompt change that fixed one thing and broke three
A dashboard you'll actually look at
practice: Interpret seven eval result comparisons
lab: Wire evals into your development loop
Evals that run automatically with a comparison report against the previous run

modules.name: Trying to Break It
modules.objective: Attack your own agent deliberately, before someone else does.
lessons: Thinking like someone who wants it to misbehave
Prompt injection through the data it reads
Making it use its tools against its purpose
Fixing a class of attack, not one instance
practice: Construct attacks against eight agent designs
lab: Red-team your own agent and fix what you find
An attack log with findings, fixes, and the re-test that confirms each fix
